Hans-Dieter Flick.style: Aggressive, front-foot football built on an extremely high defensive line and a well-drilled offside trap, usually from a 4-2-3-1. His teams press hard straight after losing the ball and attack vertically and fast rather than circulating it slowly. He is happy to trust young players.
Hans-Dieter Flick.known_for: Winning the sextuple with Bayern in 2020, then reviving Barcelona with a domestic treble in his first season, 2024-25.

Diego Simeone.style: The master of the compact, low-to-mid block, traditionally a narrow 4-4-2 that suffocates central spaces and breaks quickly. In recent years he has also used back threes and more possession, but the core is effort, aggression and game management. Famously animated on the touchline.
Diego Simeone.known_for: Turning Atlético into a power, with two La Liga titles, two Europa Leagues and two Champions League finals since 2011.

José Mourinho.style: A pragmatist who prioritises defensive organisation, opponent-specific plans and quick transitions, often from a 4-2-3-1. His sides are comfortable without the ball and ruthless on set pieces and in big games. He is a master of the psychological battle and of protecting a lead.
José Mourinho.known_for: Champions League wins with Porto (2004) and Inter (2010, as part of a treble), plus league titles in Portugal, England, Italy and Spain.

Manuel Pellegrini.style: Calm, possession-minded and attack-friendly, usually in a 4-2-3-1 or 4-4-2 with creative players given freedom between the lines. His teams build patiently and value technical quality over physical pressing. A steady, low-drama figure in the dugout.
Manuel Pellegrini.known_for: Taking Villarreal to a Champions League semi-final, winning the 2014 Premier League with Manchester City and the 2022 Copa del Rey with Betis.

Pellegrino Matarazzo.style: Energetic and pressing-focused, he has used both back-three and back-four systems with an emphasis on intensity, compactness and quick vertical attacks. Analytical and detail-oriented in preparation.
Pellegrino Matarazzo.known_for: An American coach who won promotion with Stuttgart and kept them in the Bundesliga, before a spell at Hoffenheim.

Luis García.style: Typically pragmatic and well organised, favouring a compact 4-4-2 or 4-2-3-1, a solid block and direct, efficient attacks. His teams are hard-working and hard to beat.
Luis García.known_for: A Spanish journeyman (assuming this is Luis García Plaza) with spells at Levante, Getafe, Mallorca and Alavés, where he won promotion and survival.

Quique Sánchez Flores.style: A pragmatic, defensively solid coach who prefers a compact 4-4-2 and clear structure. His teams defend in a disciplined block and look to counter or exploit set pieces.
Quique Sánchez Flores.known_for: Winning the 2010 Europa League and Super Cup with Atlético Madrid, and a long career in Spain and England, including two spells at Watford.

Edin Terzić.style: Emotional and attack-minded, usually a 4-2-3-1 or 4-3-3 with energetic pressing and quick wide combinations. His teams can be dangerous in transition and on big nights.
Edin Terzić.known_for: Winning the 2021 DFB-Pokal and reaching the 2024 Champions League final with his boyhood club Borussia Dortmund.

Claudio Giráldez.style: Brave, possession-based football, often with a back three and wing-backs, building patiently from the back and pressing high. Leans heavily on academy graduates.
Claudio Giráldez.known_for: Promoted from Celta's B team in 2024, he took the club back into Europe with a young, homegrown side.

Inigo Pérez.style: Intense, energetic football with a heavy pressing game, usually in a 4-4-2 or 4-2-3-1. His teams are aggressive, organised and work hard for each other.
Inigo Pérez.known_for: Took over Rayo Vallecano in 2024 and led them to European qualification in 2025.

Antonio Hidalgo.style: Less-known coach; his teams have tended to be well organised and competitive, with a balanced 4-4-2 or 4-2-3-1.
Antonio Hidalgo.known_for: A former midfielder who made his name coaching in Spain's second tier, notably with Huesca.

Jagoba Arrasate.style: A competitive, organised coach who likes intensity and a strong collective identity, often in a 4-4-2. His teams press, fight for second balls and are dangerous from set pieces.
Jagoba Arrasate.known_for: Leading Osasuna to the 2023 Copa del Rey final and European football, and earlier spells at Real Sociedad and Mallorca.

José López.style: Less-known coach; appears to be José Alberto López, whose sides favour possession and a proactive 4-2-3-1 or 4-3-3.
José López.known_for: A Spanish coach who has worked mainly in the second tier, with clubs including Sporting Gijón and Racing Santander.

Luís Castro.style: A possession-oriented coach who likes a 4-3-3 or 4-2-3-1, patient build-up and technical midfielders. Calm and measured on the touchline.
Luís Castro.known_for: A Portuguese coach with titles at Shakhtar Donetsk and Botafogo, and a spell at Al-Nassr.

Martín Anselmi.style: Aggressive and offensive, usually in a 3-4-3 or 3-4-2-1 with high wing-backs, man-oriented pressing and lots of bodies forward. Can leave his teams exposed at the back.
Martín Anselmi.known_for: Built his reputation at Independiente del Valle and Cruz Azul before a short spell at Porto in 2025.

Beñat San José.style: Less-known coach; generally favours an organised, possession-friendly 4-2-3-1.
Beñat San José.known_for: A Spanish coach whose career has taken him to Spain, Chile, Bolivia and the Middle East, among other places.

José Bordalás.style: Intense, physical and direct. His teams press aggressively, defend in a compact 4-4-2, foul tactically, and aim for second balls and set pieces. Loved by fans, criticised by opponents for the 'dark arts'.
José Bordalás.known_for: Taking Getafe to Europe and winning promotion with Alavés and Getafe.

Manolo González.style: Pragmatic and well organised, usually in a compact 4-4-2 or 4-2-3-1 that defends deep and strikes on the break. His teams are hard-working and hard to break down.
Manolo González.known_for: Promoted to Espanyol's first team from the B side, he won promotion in 2024 and kept the club up the following season.

Javier Aguirre.style: A pragmatic survivor who sets teams up compactly, often in a 4-4-2, with clear roles and physical commitment. Good at organising struggling sides quickly.
Javier Aguirre.known_for: A Mexican coach who has led Mexico at three World Cups and managed Osasuna, Atlético Madrid and Mallorca, reaching the 2024 Copa del Rey final.

Juan Funes.style: Less-known coach; little reliable detail about his tactical approach at senior level.
Juan Funes.known_for: A Spanish coach who worked within Málaga's structure before taking the first-team job.

Enzo Maresca.style: A Guardiola disciple who favours patient positional play, often from a 4-2-3-1 that shifts to a 3-2-4-1 or 2-3-5 in possession with an inverted full-back. Wants control and a slow, deliberate build-up.
Enzo Maresca.known_for: Winning the Championship with Leicester, then the Conference League and the 2025 Club World Cup with Chelsea.

Mikel Arteta.style: Detail-obsessed and positional, usually a 4-3-3 with a strong defensive structure, inverted full-backs and an emphasis on set pieces. His teams control games and defend aggressively.
Mikel Arteta.known_for: Rebuilding Arsenal into consistent title challengers after winning the 2020 FA Cup.

Fabian Hürzeler.style: A young, modern coach who favours possession and positional play, often in a 3-4-3 or 4-2-3-1 with fluid rotations and aggressive pressing.
Fabian Hürzeler.known_for: Won promotion to the Bundesliga with St. Pauli, then became the youngest permanent manager in Premier League history at Brighton.

Andoni Iraola.style: High-intensity, man-oriented pressing and fast, vertical attacks, usually from a 4-2-3-1 or 4-4-2. His teams run hard and look to win the ball high.
Andoni Iraola.known_for: Turned Rayo Vallecano and then Bournemouth into energetic, overachieving sides.

Xabi Alonso.style: Positional and possession-based, often a 3-4-2-1 with wing-backs providing width and two creative 10s. His teams are flexible, well-drilled and dangerous in transition.
Xabi Alonso.known_for: Leading Bayer Leverkusen to an unbeaten Bundesliga and DFB-Pokal double in 2023-24, before taking the Real Madrid job in 2025.

Keith Andrews.style: Less-known as a head coach; came up as a set-piece specialist and is expected to keep Brentford's aggressive, direct and set-piece-heavy style.
Keith Andrews.known_for: A former Ireland midfielder who was Brentford's set-piece coach before being promoted to head coach in 2025.

Daniel Farke.style: Possession-based football in a 4-2-3-1 or 4-3-3, with patient build-up and attacking full-backs. His teams dominate the ball, especially in the Championship.
Daniel Farke.known_for: Won the Championship twice with Norwich and earned promotion with Leeds.

Matthias Jaissle.style: Red Bull school: aggressive pressing, quick transitions and vertical attacks, often in a 4-2-2-2 or 4-3-1-2.
Matthias Jaissle.known_for: Won the Austrian title with Red Bull Salzburg and the AFC Champions League Elite with Al-Ahli in 2025.

Unai Emery.style: Obsessively detailed and highly adaptable, usually a 4-4-2 or 4-2-3-1 with a high defensive line and a well-coached offside trap. He prepares specific plans for every opponent and is especially strong in knockout football.
Unai Emery.known_for: A record four Europa League titles (three with Sevilla, one with Villarreal) and taking Aston Villa back into the Champions League.

Sergej Jakirović.style: Organised and competitive, usually in a 4-2-3-1, with an emphasis on balance and transitions.
Sergej Jakirović.known_for: A Bosnian-Croatian coach who won the domestic double with Dinamo Zagreb in 2024 before moving to Hull.

David Moyes.style: Pragmatic and well organised, often in a 4-2-3-1 or back three. His teams are solid, compact, strong in the air and dangerous on the break and from set pieces.
David Moyes.known_for: Eleven years at Everton, a short spell at Manchester United and winning the 2023 Conference League with West Ham.

Gary O'Neil.style: Flexible and tactically adaptable, often switching between back three and back four depending on opponents. His teams are organised and quick on the counter.
Gary O'Neil.known_for: Kept Bournemouth up and then overachieved with Wolves.

Marco Rose.style: Red Bull-style pressing and quick vertical attacks, often in a 4-2-2-2 or 3-4-2-1. His teams are aggressive and dangerous in transition.
Marco Rose.known_for: Won the UEFA Youth League and Austrian titles with Salzburg and the 2023 DFB-Pokal with RB Leipzig.

Roberto De Zerbi.style: Possession-based with a distinctive 'baiting' build-up, inviting the press with slow passes before breaking through it, often in a 4-2-3-1 or 4-1-4-1. Demanding, passionate and stubborn about his principles.
Roberto De Zerbi.known_for: Transformed Brighton with innovative build-up play and led them into Europe for the first time, after spells at Sassuolo and Shakhtar Donetsk.

Álvaro Arbeloa.style: Less-known as a senior coach; his youth teams at Real Madrid played attacking, possession-based football in a 4-3-3.
Álvaro Arbeloa.known_for: A former Real Madrid and Spain full-back who won trophies with Real Madrid's youth sides before stepping up to senior management.

Michael Carrick.style: Possession-based and calm, usually a 4-2-3-1 with patient build-up and full-backs pushing on. A measured presence on the touchline.
Michael Carrick.known_for: A former Manchester United and England midfielder who built a good reputation at Middlesbrough.

Pierre Sage.style: Less-known coach; at Lyon his teams combined possession with aggressive pressing, often in a 4-3-3.
Pierre Sage.known_for: Promoted from Lyon's academy in 2023, he turned around a struggling team and led it to the 2024 Coupe de France final and European qualification.

Oliver Glasner.style: A 3-4-2-1 or 3-4-3 with intense pressing, quick transitions and wing-backs carrying the width. His teams are direct and dangerous on the break, and he is strong in cup football.
Oliver Glasner.known_for: Winning the 2022 Europa League with Eintracht Frankfurt and the 2025 FA Cup with Crystal Palace.

Frank Lampard.style: Attacking intent in a 4-2-3-1 or 4-3-3, with runners from midfield and a willingness to trust young players.
Frank Lampard.known_for: A Chelsea legend who managed Derby, Chelsea and Everton.

Régis Le Bris.style: Possession-minded and patient, often a 4-2-3-1 with young players given responsibility and a calm, structured approach.
Régis Le Bris.known_for: Led Sunderland to Premier League promotion in 2025 after a spell at Lorient.

Vincent Kompany.style: Brave, possession-heavy football with a very high line, aggressive pressing and full-backs stepping into midfield, usually from a 4-2-3-1. Wants control and constant pressure.
Vincent Kompany.known_for: Won the Championship with Burnley in 2023 and the Bundesliga in his first season at Bayern.

Niko Kovač.style: Pragmatic and physically demanding, often in a back three or 4-2-3-1, with an emphasis on defensive solidity and transitions.
Niko Kovač.known_for: Won the 2018 DFB-Pokal with Eintracht Frankfurt and the 2019 double with Bayern Munich.

Julian Schuster.style: Continues Freiburg's well-organised, flexible approach, switching between back three and back four with an emphasis on defensive structure and collective effort.
Julian Schuster.known_for: A Freiburg club legend as a player who succeeded Christian Streich as head coach in 2024.

Carles Martínez.style: Less-known coach; little reliable detail available about his tactical approach.
Carles Martínez.known_for: A Spanish coach in Leverkusen's dugout; his background is not widely documented.

Martín Demichelis.style: Positional, possession-based football inspired by Guardiola, usually in a 4-2-3-1 or 4-3-3 with full-backs pushing on.
Martín Demichelis.known_for: A former Bayern and Manchester City defender who won the Argentine title with River Plate in 2023.

Daniel Thioune.style: Organised and competitive, usually in a 4-3-3 or 4-2-3-1, with a mix of possession and intensity.
Daniel Thioune.known_for: Won promotion with Osnabrück and Fortuna Düsseldorf and had a spell at Hamburg.

Urs Fischer.style: Compact, disciplined defending in a 3-5-2 or 5-3-2, with quick counters and strong set pieces. His teams are well organised and hard to beat.
Urs Fischer.known_for: Took Union Berlin from the 2. Bundesliga to the Champions League, after winning Swiss titles with Basel.

Vincent Wagner.style: Less-known coach; at Elversberg he is expected to continue the club's attacking, possession-based style.
Vincent Wagner.known_for: A young German coach who worked as an assistant before becoming Elversberg's head coach.

Manuel Baum.style: A thoughtful, analytical coach, often with a back three and a mix of possession and counter-attacking football.
Manuel Baum.known_for: Kept Augsburg in the Bundesliga during his first spell (2016 to 2019) and has worked in youth development, including for the German FA.

Christian Ilzer.style: Aggressive pressing and quick vertical attacks, often in a 4-4-2 diamond or 3-4-3. His teams play with intensity and energy.
Christian Ilzer.known_for: Won the Austrian double with Sturm Graz in 2024, ending Salzburg's long dominance.

Merlin Polzin.style: A young coach who favours possession and attacking football, often in a 4-3-3 or 3-4-3.
Merlin Polzin.known_for: Led Hamburg back to the Bundesliga in 2025 after stepping up from assistant coach.

Rene Wagner.style: Less-known coach; little reliable detail about his approach as a head coach.
Rene Wagner.known_for: A German coach promoted to lead Köln; previously worked as an assistant.

Ralf Kettemann.style: Less-known coach; little reliable detail about his tactical approach.
Ralf Kettemann.known_for: A German coach who took charge of Paderborn.

Adolf Hütter.style: Energetic pressing and fast vertical attacks, often in a 3-4-2-1 or 4-2-2-2. His teams are aggressive and direct.
Adolf Hütter.known_for: Won the Swiss title with Young Boys in 2018 and led Eintracht Frankfurt to the 2019 Europa League semi-finals.

Sebastian Hoeneß.style: Possession-minded and flexible, often a 4-2-3-1 or 3-4-2-1 with good ball circulation and attacking full-backs.
Sebastian Hoeneß.known_for: Led Stuttgart from relegation battles to second place in 2024 and the 2025 DFB-Pokal.

Miron Muslić.style: Energetic and aggressive, with a focus on pressing and quick attacks, often using a back three.
Miron Muslić.known_for: Made his name at Cercle Brugge before spells at Plymouth and Schalke.

Mauro Lustrinelli.style: Less-known coach; at Thun and with the Swiss under-21s his teams played organised, attacking football.
Mauro Lustrinelli.known_for: A former Swiss international striker who coached Thun and the Switzerland under-21s.

Alexander Blessin.style: Red Bull-style pressing and quick transitions, often in a 4-2-2-2 or 3-4-3. His teams are aggressive and intense.
Alexander Blessin.known_for: Coached Ostend, Genoa, Union Saint-Gilloise and St. Pauli.

Luis Enrique.style: Intense positional football with relentless pressing, usually a 4-3-3 with full-backs pushing very high and forwards swapping positions. He prioritises collective work over stars.
Luis Enrique.known_for: Won trebles with Barcelona in 2015 and PSG in 2025, including the club's first Champions League.

Cesc Fàbregas.style: Possession-dominant, positional football inspired by his Barcelona and Arsenal roots, often a 4-2-3-1 with technical players and patient build-up.
Cesc Fàbregas.known_for: A Spain and Arsenal great who led Como back to Serie A and quickly established them in the top flight.

Ivan Leko.style: Organised and aggressive, often a 4-3-3 or 3-4-3 with high pressing and quick transitions.
Ivan Leko.known_for: Won the Belgian title with Club Brugge in 2018.

Rui Borges.style: Flexible and attack-minded, often a back three with wing-backs and quick combinations.
Rui Borges.known_for: Won the Portuguese double with Sporting CP in 2025 after making his name at Vitória Guimarães.

Gian Piero Gasperini.style: A 3-4-2-1 with man-to-man marking all over the pitch, intense physical demands and aggressive wing-backs. His teams are relentless, direct and attack-minded.
Gian Piero Gasperini.known_for: Turned Atalanta into a Champions League regular and won the 2024 Europa League.

Arda Turan.style: Less-known as a coach; favours attacking, possession-based football with technical players.
Arda Turan.known_for: A Turkey and Atlético Madrid great who won promotion with Eyüpspor before taking the Shakhtar job in 2025.

Peter Bosz.style: Attacking, possession-based football with intense counter-pressing and a high line, usually in a 4-3-3. His teams take risks and score lots of goals.
Peter Bosz.known_for: Reached the 2017 Europa League final with Ajax and won back-to-back Eredivisie titles with PSV in 2024 and 2025.

Cristian Chivu.style: A young coach who favours an organised back three with wing-backs, mixing compact defending with quick attacks.
Cristian Chivu.known_for: A former Inter and Roma defender who coached Inter's youth team and kept Parma in Serie A before taking the Inter job in 2025.

Massimiliano Allegri.style: A pragmatic game manager who values balance, defensive solidity and control over style, often switching between back three and back four. His teams are often dull but effective.
Massimiliano Allegri.known_for: Won six Serie A titles with Juventus (five in a row) and one with Milan, and reached two Champions League finals.

Okan Buruk.style: Attack-minded in a 4-2-3-1 with star players given freedom, combining possession and quick transitions.
Okan Buruk.known_for: Won Süper Lig titles with Başakşehir in 2020 and Galatasaray in 2023, 2024 and 2025.

Dietmar Kühbauer.style: Passionate and demanding, his teams are compact, organised and physically strong, often in a 4-4-2 or 3-4-3.
Dietmar Kühbauer.known_for: An Austrian coach who has worked with Rapid Vienna, Wolfsberger AC and LASK.

Valdas Dambrauskas.style: Less-known coach; his teams are typically organised and attack-minded.
Valdas Dambrauskas.known_for: A Lithuanian coach who won titles with Riga FC and coached Ludogorets in Bulgaria. (FotMob's squad page lists no coach for Sabah; this name comes from its coach history.)

Giovanni van Bronckhorst.style: Possession-minded and organised, usually in a 4-3-3 or 4-2-3-1 with attacking full-backs.
Giovanni van Bronckhorst.known_for: Won the Eredivisie with Feyenoord in 2017 and reached the 2022 Europa League final with Rangers.

Yannick Cahuzac.style: Less-known coach; little reliable detail about his tactical approach as a head coach.
Yannick Cahuzac.known_for: A former midfielder who played for Bastia and Lens before moving into coaching.

Kjetil Knutsen.style: Attacking, possession-based football in a 4-3-3 with intense pressing and quick combinations. His teams are fearless and very fit.
Kjetil Knutsen.known_for: Turned Bodø/Glimt into Norwegian champions and led them to the 2025 Europa League semi-finals.

Marko Nikolić.style: Organised and competitive, often in a 4-2-3-1, with an emphasis on defensive balance and transitions.
Marko Nikolić.known_for: A Serbian coach who won the Russian Cup with Lokomotiv Moscow and has managed Partizan and AEK Athens.

İsmail Kartal.style: Attack-minded and organised, often in a 4-2-3-1, with an emphasis on quick wide play.
İsmail Kartal.known_for: Led Fenerbahçe to a 99-point season in 2023-24, finishing second to Galatasaray.

Jindřich Trpišovský.style: High-intensity, man-oriented pressing and physical, direct football, often in a 3-4-3 or 4-2-3-1. His teams are aggressive and very fit.
Jindřich Trpišovský.known_for: Won multiple Czech titles with Slavia Prague and took them to two Europa League quarter-finals.

Morten Jensen.style: Less-known coach; little reliable detail about his tactical approach.
Morten Jensen.known_for: A Danish coach working at Viking in Norway.

Francesco Farioli.style: Possession-based positional play with a very structured build-up, often in a 4-3-3. His teams defend well and control games.
Francesco Farioli.known_for: Made his name at Nice and came close to the Eredivisie title with Ajax in 2025.

Davide Ancelotti.style: Less-known as a head coach; schooled as his father Carlo's assistant, he favours a balanced, flexible approach.
Davide Ancelotti.known_for: Long-time assistant to Carlo Ancelotti at Bayern, Napoli, Everton and Real Madrid, before his first head-coach job at Botafogo in 2025.

Yaya Touré.style: Less-known as a head coach; little reliable detail about his tactical approach.
Yaya Touré.known_for: A Manchester City and Barcelona great as a player who has since worked in coaching roles, including as an assistant with Saudi Arabia.
